pull: Clue: Londoners named it after an insect
body:
Can you name this weapon?

On 5 December 1943, American B-26 Marauders began bombing the launch sites being built for it in northern France, the start of the long Allied campaign code named Crossbow. The raids helped push back its first use by months. It finally fell on London in June 1944.

The clue is on the card. Drop your guess below.
photoNote: A complete V-1 that came down without exploding in France, found by the Ninth Air Force; print received January 1945, so taken in late 1944, a year after the event. U.S. Air Force 61375AC, NARA 342-FH-3A16599 (NAID 204890590). Tier: green, U.S. government work, public domain. Cropped to the photo, removing the print's caption, stamps, and number. No markings name it.
photoCredit: A V-1 flying bomb that landed intact in France, found by the U.S. Ninth Air Force, 1944. U.S. Air Force 61375AC, National Archives, public domain.
